thread:
erin: Quick sync — we need a concrete per-org rate policy spec for RPM/TPM + concurrency caps. current doc is high level and product wants a proposal for next week's roadmap review.
sam: Ack. Do we already prefer TPM (= tokens per minute) over RPM for fairness? feels more cost-aligned.
erin: Product wants both. TPM for billing/cost; RPM for protecting control plane (API request floods). Concurrency caps are separate SLOs.
katie: agree. proposal idea: dual-limits: 1) org-level TPM rolling window (60s) 2) org-level RPM (60s) 3) org concurrency cap (in-flight requests). plus a small "burst allowance".
ryan: what does "burst allowance" mean operationally? sliding window with token bucket?
erin: My thought: token-bucket per org for short bursts (e.g., 2x baseline for up to 10s), then smooth to steady-state rate. prevents small spikes from hitting hard caps.
sam: want to call out percentiles on telemetry. We should emit: tokens_used_1m, requests_1m, inflight_current, burst_seconds_remaining. dashboards need those.
katie: also need per-route multipliers. embeddings are heavy tokens but low QPS; chat is many small calls. allow route-level weight so TPM reflects cost.
ryan: edge case: service accounts / infra integrations that fan out many requests. We need per-key overrides or tiered quotas. How do we authenticate? org-owner can whitelist keys for higher concurrency.
erin: yes, have administrative override flag (requires audit log). Also plan for rate tiering: default free tier X, paid tier Y, enterprise custom.
sam: enforcement point? API gateway should reject early for RPM, but TPM requires inspecting body (tokens) — expensive at gateway.
katie: gateway can estimate token cost with a heuristic (prompt length + model factor) and emit for accurate accounting at runtime. if gateway estimate > quota then reject, else let pass and reconcile.
ryan: reconciliation can trigger soft-blocks if org exceeded after accounting, with grace TTL to allow quick backoff. need consistent metric ordering to avoid races.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: rate-limiter v2 -> canary (10%) at 2026-02-15T03:00Z.
erin: Rollout plan: start with monitoring-only for 1 day, then rejection mode for 1% of orgs for 24h, then 10% for 48h, then ramp to 100% with 2-hour pause windows. send org-owner notifications on rejection.
sam: UX: console should show current usage vs quota, estimate of next-minute burn, and a simulated "what-if" slider for request bursts. also surface which route consumed tokens.
katie: metrics to implement: org/tokens_1m_rate, org/requests_1m_rate, org/inflight_peak_1m, org/burst_credit. unit tests + load test harness to verify fairness.
ryan: corner case: multi-tenant infra accounts where a single org spawns many sub-orgs (teams). probably need per-subkey sub-limits and an aggregate org cap.
erin: agreed. action items: Sam -> telemetry metrics + dashboard mocks by Friday. Katie -> config schema + gateway estimation algorithm. Ryan -> enforcement plan and canary gating. I'll write rollout doc and notification templates.
sam: I'll add example dashboard panels and an alert rule for tokens_1m > 90% sustained for 5m.
katie: sample config snippet for discussion:
```
org_quota: 
  tpm: 120000 
  rpm: 2000
  concurrency: 50
  burst_multiplier: 2
  burst_max_seconds: 10
  route_weights: 
    /v1/chat: 1
    /v1/embeddings: 3
```
ryan: lgtm. one more: fallback policy. When exceeded, prefer model downgrade (smaller quantized model) first, then shared fallback pool, then hard reject. keep 429 body with reason and "retry-after" seconds.
erin: nice. also include webhook to customer when they hit hard reject 3x in an hour.
sam: cool. I'll start the dashboard PR.
katie: I'll prototype the gateway estimator and unit tests.
ryan: I'll draft the canary gating rules and the safety kill-switch runbook.
erin: thanks team. I'll consolidate into spec and post in #eng-platform for comments before Friday. :thumbsup:
